bug_semantics: OpenAM 16.0.6 installs the iPlanetDirectoryPro SSO cookie with com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false and com.iplanet.am.cookie.secure=false and without a SameSite default. Its OAuth2/OIDC consent path also exposed that same session identifier to JavaScript and treated it as the csrf form value. Consequently, same-origin script execution could read and replay the bearer session, and could satisfy the consent check with the stolen session identifier; the missing SameSite and protocol-derived Secure defaults widened cross-site and transport exposure.
flaw_origin: The smallest non-move commit that first wrote the advisory-specific SSO-token-as-CSRF mechanism is 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88. It created openam-oauth2/src/main/java/org/forgerock/oauth2/core/CsrfProtection.java with ssoToken.getTokenID().toString() as the expected csrf value, created OAuth2ConsentPageHelper.js to read the configured SSO cookie through CookieHelper.getCookie, and changed main-authorize.js to submit that value. Earlier insecure cookie defaults existed in the migrated codebase, but their first appearances in this Git history are copy/move imports and therefore are not valid BICs under the protocol; 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88 is the first reconstructable direct commit that completed the consent-specific vulnerable coupling removed by the patch.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object names human author Phill Cunnington <phill.cunnington@forgerock.com> and human committer Joe Bandenburg <joe.bandenburg@forgerock.com>; its complete message is exactly 'OPENAM-8575' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/OpenIdentityPlatform/OpenAM/security/advisories/GHSA-fpmh-vx4h-xc33 identifies affected versions through 16.0.6, patched version 16.1.1, HttpOnly=false, missing SameSite, and reuse of iPlanetDirectoryPro as the OAuth/OIDC csrf value. At tag 16.0.6 (4529f108e9f5d3b8f98b4afb3dd035a3c4d73a1b), openam-server-only/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/template/sms/serverdefaults.properties contains com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false and com.iplanet.am.cookie.secure=false, while CsrfProtection.isCsrfAttack reads ssoToken.getTokenID().toString() and compares it to request parameter csrf. `git log -L 44,50:openam-oauth2/src/main/java/org/forgerock/oauth2/core/CsrfProtection.java 97a34d9fee17395e8e052bfc45eb5855f436153e` traces those vulnerable lines directly to 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88; `git log -S 'getTokenID().toString()' -- .../CsrfProtection.java` independently returns that introducer and the later fix. The BIC creates CsrfProtection.java and OAuth2ConsentPageHelper.js; the latter returns CookieHelper.getCookie(config.cookieName), and main-authorize.js places that session id into data.oauth2Data.csrf. Direct parent-tree checks against 3c076fc0dd1142d3c69fa39985667da2e1a8b628 find no CsrfProtection.java and no getTokenID().toString() coupling, proving immediate-parent absence. `git cat-file commit 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88` supplies the human identities and trailer-free one-line message quoted in ai_marker. Direct fix 2af597267e6eb9302f75445c2c726f9b84f62966 (https://github.com/OpenIdentityPlatform/OpenAM/commit/2af597267e6eb9302f75445c2c726f9b84f62966) replaces session-id comparison with a dedicated random token stored as a protected session property or HttpOnly double-submit cookie, stops main-authorize.js from reading the SSO cookie for consent, adds SameSite=Lax, and derives Secure from HTTPS. Its parent 97a34d9fee17395e8e052bfc45eb5855f436153e still contains the vulnerable comparison and lacks the SameSite installation default. The advisory-linked 16.1.1 release tag resolves to fe2271ec119e827b4252cec20293480322a84789 (https://github.com/OpenIdentityPlatform/OpenAM/releases/tag/16.1.1). Ancestry checks show the BIC is contained in 16.0.6, the direct fix is not contained in 16.0.6, and the direct fix is contained in 16.1.1.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle has two layers: longstanding permissive SSO-cookie initialization, plus the 2016 consent implementation that made the bearer session identifier itself the CSRF secret and caused browser code to read it. The historical occurrences of the old cookie-default code arrive through the repository's 2012 module-copy migration (for example, 94cdb6ea929e1d7232a268aacb435b86cb78a787 is explicitly 'moved tempolate into webapp'), so treating those moves as introducers would violate the audit protocol. Commit 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88 is instead a real, atomic feature commit: it creates both sides of the exact consent coupling and its parent lacks them. The 16.0.6 tree demonstrates the coupling coexisting with HttpOnly=false/Secure=false and no SameSite default. Commit 2af597267e6eb9302f75445c2c726f9b84f62966 directly breaks that coupling and hardens the defaults before the advisory's 16.1.1 boundary at fe2271ec119e827b4252cec20293480322a84789. Because attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object, later release-note references to Copilot and any AI involvement in unrelated release commits or fixes are irrelevant. The BIC object has only named human author/committer identities and no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
